The prayers made, and the relief sought in Petition No. 378/MP/2022 and Petition No. 220/MP/2022 are similar, and the petitions are based on the corrigendum issued by CEA on 29.3.2022 to the TEC of ISHEP. Therefore, both the said petitions are dealt with together in the instant order. 7. After hearing the submissions of the Petitioner, the Commission admitted Petition No. 220/MP/2022 on 11.12.2022 and Petition No. 378/MP/2022 on 11.4.2023 and issued notice to the Respondents and directed the parties to complete the pleadings. 10. The final hearing in these matters was held on 17.10.2025, and the order was reserved. This order is being passed on the basis of the submissions made by the Petitioner vide affidavits dated 9.3.2023, 1.5.2023, 2.5.2023, 19.5.2023, 30.10.2023, 201.11.2023, 14.12.2023, 5.4.2024, 19.8.2025 and 7.11.2025. 11. The gist of the submissions made by the Petitioner in the case of ISHEP in Petition No.378/MP/2022 are as follows: (c) The Petitioner disclosed that it has filed a Writ Petition before the High Court of Madhya Pradesh challenging certain provisions of the Tariff Regulations and seeking revision of Design Energy. The relief sought therein substantially overlaps with the relief claimed in the present Petition, thereby amounting to parallel proceedings for similar relief. Simultaneous pursuit of remedies constitutes forum shopping and is impermissible under the law. The attempt to differentiate the reliefs is artificial, as the substantive objective in both proceedings is revision of Design Energy and consequential financial impact. (e) The Petitioner is, in effect, seeking review and reopening of tariff orders pertaining to earlier control periods, which have attained finality and were never challenged within the limitation. The present attempt is therefore barred by delay and laches. (h) Both parties have acted upon the tariff orders and finalised their financial affairs accordingly. Billing, revenue realisation, tax payments, including MAT adjustments, and dividend declarations have been completed based on approved accounts. ## **Rejoinder and additional submissions of the Petitioner in Petition No. 378/MP/2022** (b) The relief sought in the Writ Petition filed before the Hon’ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh is in a different legal context and pertains to separate regulatory issues. The present petition concerns the correction of tariff computation within the Commission's jurisdiction and therefore does not overlap in substance. (c) As regards the allegation of forum shopping, the invocation of remedies before different fora for distinct causes of action is legally permissible. The mere existence of another proceeding does not render the present petition impermissible. (h) As regards the contention that the parties have acted upon earlier tariff orders and finalised their financial affairs, the administrative finality cannot ## **Rejoinder and written submissions of the Petitioner in Petition No. 220/MP/2022** 16. The gist of the submissions made by the Petitioner in its rejoinder and written submissions is as follows: (e) The Writ Petition filed before the Hon’ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh pertains to distinct reliefs, including revision of Design Energy and refund of Secondary Energy charges, and that the issues raised before the Commission fall squarely within its statutory jurisdiction over tariff determination. 25. We have scrutinised the information submitted by the Petitioner, and it is observed that excess secondary charges were recovered from the Petitioner. The Petitioner had paid excess secondary energy charges to NHDC on account of the incorrect consideration of the unit of water utilisation for irrigation ‘Q’ as BM[3] instead of MFAt by CEA in its TEC in respect of ISHEP and the Commission in its tariff orders. We are of the view that the Petitioner had paid excess secondary charges for no fault of its own, and the Petitioner should be refunded the same. As a mere revision and computation of Firm Power and Design Energy as sought by the Petitioner would not restore the Petitioner to the same economic position, the Commission sought the details from the Petitioner, which have been submitted by the Petitioner, to confirm whether the Petitioner has paid excess secondary energy charges. We are of the considered view that it is just and equitable to return the excess secondary energy charges recovered from the Petitioner. Therefore, NHDC’s contention that no consequential relief should be allowed to the Petitioner, as no prayer to that effect is made by it, is rejected. 27. We have considered the submissions of NHDC and Petitioner. In the Writ Petition before the Hon’ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh, the Petitioner has challenged the tariff regulations imposing the secondary energy charges on the Petitioner, however, in the instant petitions, the Petitioner is seeking the revision of Firm Power and Design Energy and the consequent secondary energy charges on the basis of the Corrigendum issued by CEA correcting the ‘Q’ from BM[3] to MFAt. Moreover, the Petitioner is seeking retrospective revision of the Firm Power and Design Energy from 2010-11 onwards in the instant petitions. Thus, the relief sought in the Writ Petition before the Hon’ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh is different from the relief sought in the instant petitions. issued to end the dispute between the parties.
